threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You call it a 'corner shop' instead of a 'newsagent' and don't know the unwritten rule about queuing at the post office. Classic rookie move.
Heard a couple arguing about who left the last bottle of wine at the bus stop. Turns out it was a bottle of vinegar. Classic Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy set up a mobile disco in the park, blasting techno while kids flew kites. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you get a döner and simultaneously hear a live band jamming in the street. It's like a perfect soundtrack to late-night snacking.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who's from here by how they get annoyed at tourists taking selfies in front of the Mission murals during rush hour.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 19 Polk singing opera to a packed bus. Everyone went from annoyed to entertained in seconds. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but it’s the cendros on Carrer de Verdi that hum with real local life, especially at dusk.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newbie by their map fixation—standing on the corner of Carrer de València, searching for directions like it’s a treasure map.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions to the nearest Tube station instead of just hopping on the Overground from Dalston Junction.
Caught a woman knitting a scarf on the 37 last night. She had a little bag of wool and seemed completely unfazed by the drunk crowd.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid proudly showing off their new skateboard at the Grafitti wall, totally unbothered by the world around them. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice that even during a BVG strike, people still find a way to get around? A bike share and an umbrella usually do the trick.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know that the taco stand at 24th and Valencia is always better after a late-night bar crawl. Only tourists go for the trendy spots.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today where the driver stopped to let a saxophonist play a solo. Only in SF would a jam session break out mid-commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the bars here close at 2 AM. Nah, in Gràcia, the real night just starts heating up around 3 AM with locals gathering for xampanyet.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They linger way too long at the metro ticket machines, still figuring out the options instead of just tapping their cards.
